title: The Political Favour
setup: A local councillor approaches you with a smile. He's helped people in this area — got a road fixed, released a wrongly detained teenager. He's also known to take cuts on contracts. He offers to 'smooth things over' with a bureaucratic problem you've been stuck on for two weeks. 'Just call it mutual support,' he says.

personaContext.arjun_das: Two weeks of bounced calls. The councillor can end this in a phone call. Arjun knows the system runs on this. Participating makes him part of it.
personaContext.priya_mondal: This is her world. She knows this councillor personally. She also knows exactly what the 'mutual support' will cost her later.
personaContext.ramesh_paswan: He has no leverage in this system. But accepting creates a debt. He's been in debt to people like this before.
personaContext.siddharth_roy: He's done this. He calls it 'networking'. The reframing is getting harder to maintain.
personaContext.nasreen_begum: She's seen what 'mutual support' does to communities over five years. She also has three families whose cases are stuck in the same system.

choices.text: Accept. 'I appreciate it, Kaka. Whatever I can do to help in return.' The problem gets resolved.
choices.narrativeOutcome: The problem disappears in 48 hours. The councillor calls once more, casually. 'I told my nephew you might have time this week.' You understand the currency now.

choices.text: Decline with a smile. 'Thank you dada, but I think I'll try the normal process a few more times.'
choices.narrativeOutcome: He nods, smile intact. 'Of course, of course.' You've preserved your integrity and extended your wait by at least three weeks. The system rewards patience inversely to need.

choices.text: Say yes, but use the access to also push through two others' stuck cases. Use it broadly.
choices.narrativeOutcome: All three cases resolve. The councillor raises an eyebrow at the additions. 'You're thorough.' You've bent the system but also redistributed its benefits. The debt is larger now.

choices.text: Decline and document the offer. This is an opportunity to expose how the system works.
choices.narrativeOutcome: You write it up. Two people share it. The councillor calls to say 'there has been a misunderstanding.' Your problem remains unsolved. You've made an enemy with a long memory.
